extracted.intended_audience: researchers reporting in vivo animal studies; journal editors and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on what to report when describing animal (in vivo) experiments to ensure transparency, reproducibility, and assessment of reliability. Covers a prioritized Essential 10 minimum reporting items and a Recommended Set of additional contextual items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Design
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 1 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Part of the 'basic minimum' information that must be included in any manuscript describing animal research so readers and reviewers can assess reliability of the findings. (Detailed explanations and examples available on individual item pages / Explanation and Elaboration paper.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 2 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Considered part of the minimum reporting necessary for assessment of study reliability. (See item-specific guidance and examples in the full guidelines.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 3 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Must be reported to allow appraisal of how subjects/units were selected and whether post-hoc exclusions occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 4 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Report randomisation methods used to allocate animals to groups to allow assessment of bias minimisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 5 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Report whether and how blinding was implemented to reduce observer or assessment bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 6 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Report primary and secondary outcome measures so readers can judge relevance and interpretation of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 7 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Report statistical approaches and any assumptions to allow evaluation of analyses and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental animals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 8 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Report characteristics of animals used (species, strain, sex, age, weight, etc.) to enable interpretation and replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 9 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Provide sufficient detail of procedures and interventions to allow replication and assessment of potential sources of variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 10 of the ARRIVE Essential 10. Present results transparently so readers and reviewers can assess reliability; reporting the Essential 10 is described as the basic minimum required to assess findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 11 in the Recommended Set. These items complement the Essential 10 and add important context; reporting both sets is recommended best practice. Abstract should summarise key methodological and outcome information per guidance in full ARRIVE documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 12 in the Recommended Set. Provide scientific context and rationale for the study as part of best-practice reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 13 in the Recommended Set. Clearly state hypotheses or objectives to contextualise design and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical statement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 14 in the Recommended Set. Report approvals and ethical oversight to demonstrate compliance with animal welfare standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and husbandry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 15 in the Recommended Set. Describe housing, enrichment, and husbandry conditions which can affect experimental outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 16 in the Recommended Set. Report monitoring, humane endpoints, analgesia/anaesthesia, and care practices relevant to welfare and data quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation/ scientific implications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 17 in the Recommended Set. Discuss how results fit with existing knowledge, limitations, and implications for further research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability/ translation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 18 in the Recommended Set. Report considerations about applicability of findings to other species, models, or clinical translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol registration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 19 in the Recommended Set. Report whether the study protocol was registered or pre-specified to increase transparency and reduce selective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 20 in the Recommended Set. Provide information on availability of data and materials to enable verification and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of interests
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 21 in the Recommended Set. Disclose funding sources and potential conflicts of interest to allow readers to judge possible biases.
